scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Approximate counting of common bases of two matroids” (preprints/Approximate-counting-of-common-bases-of-two-matroids-September-23-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 114 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 7ed3dfdefcfa677a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a single randomized oracle algorithm with the following guarantee. Given independence oracles for arbitrary rank-r matroids M1, M2 on [n], and rational ϵ, δ ∈ (0, 1), it outputs a nonnegative rational b Z such that P  (1 − ϵ)Z(M1, M2) ≤ b Z ≤ (1 + ϵ)Z(M1, M2)  ≥ 1 − δ. If Z(M1, M2) = 0, its output is always zero. On every execution, the number of oracle calls and the number of other bit operations are bounded by a fixed polynomial in n, ℓ, ϵ−1 , log δ−1 , where ℓ is the binary encoding length of n, r, ϵ, δ. The algorithm uses only independent unbiased random bits and does not require a representation of either matroid.
